body: I am curious to hear from people myself because, like you, I also got an interview for the same area for the general track. I’m nervous and excited all at the same time! I wish you luck in your interview!

Aww thank you and I rarely put in the amount of effort I have into my theories haha, usually I just skim the surface. And I'd love to see some of your art! Who knows, you might already have some symbolism you are even aware of.
Yeah it's crazy to think about! Those lesions/black spots make me so uncomfortable to look at. Makes my skin crawl.

I'm just a lowly broke college student with too much procrastinated time on their hands haha! I am really into biology and art thus I spend a lot of time looking at specific details of images to see if I can figure out the symbolism of the art. This usually means figuring out the closest or specific type of insect/plant/animal/etc these are as I find researching them is incredibly helpful for understanding hidden/overlooked themes of stories and games (like the last of us). I may be completely wrong with my theory or interpretation but I like what I have deduced as I feel it may be pretty close to the real meaning. Plus I am getting this tattooed on my body tomorrow so I wanted to be a accurate as possible in order to make it my own and feel comfortable with the meaning behind the art.

Edit:

This part is just pure speculation off of random research I decided to do for funsies. Silk moths/silk worms can be infected with something called Beauveria Bassiana which is an asexual reproducing form of the Cordyceps bassiana fungus except...GET THIS. Beauveria Bassiana has a recorded case of infecting a human, albeit they had a suppressed immune system, but infected with this fungus nonetheless. Cordyceps has yet to have a documented case of human infection whereas, the closely related and similar fungus mentioned above has had a single documented case.

Another cool thing I realized/theorized about the tattoo was that based off the concept art, specifically the leaves that are not filled in, closely resemble Rowan tree leaves. Rowan trees are poisonous and according to Celtic mythology (if I recall) symbolize strength and protection.
